site.tagline: Scheduling for people who get paid
site.description: Publish event types, take free or paid bookings, and run memberships from a hosted page or embed. Built for coaches, clinics, consultants, tutors, salons, and trainers.

footer.blurb: Scheduling for people who get paid. Publish the offer, share a page or embed, get booked — and paid — in one flow.
footer.meta: Cards stay on Stripe. Time stays in UTC. Money is integer cents.

home.heroLead: Publish event types, share a hosted page or embed, and take free sessions, paid bookings, or memberships — without the email tennis.
home.heroNote: Free forever for unpaid bookings. Pro is $29/mo the day you attach a price. Cards stay on Stripe.
home.heroVisualSr: Animated preview of a hosted booking page: a client picks Thursday the 24th at 10:30 am and pays $120 through Stripe Checkout. Card data never touches SchedFlow.
home.productTitle: A booking page that can settle up, not just find a time.
home.productLead: Calendly-shaped scheduling with Stripe Connect in the same motion — for practices that charge for the hour.
home.howTitle: Five moves from empty calendar to paid session.
home.paymentsTitle: The slot is not yours until Checkout completes.
home.paymentsLead: Connect Express for payouts. A 15-minute hold so two people cannot buy the same hour. A 2% application fee on connected charges — not on your Pro subscription.
home.plansTitle: Free until you charge. Pro the day you do.
home.plansLead: No trial. Stay on Free indefinitely. Upgrade self-serve when a paid event type or membership is the next step.
home.faqLead: No trial. No enterprise invoice. Self-serve Free or Pro, and a 2% fee only on money that runs through Connect.

paid.title: Price the slot. Hold it. Checkout.
paid.body: Paid event types lock the interval for 15 minutes while the invitee finishes Stripe Checkout. Abandoned payments expire. The hour goes back on the board.

credits.title: Memberships, not just one-offs
credits.body: Period credits for tutors and trainers. Clients buy a plan, book without paying per visit, and refill when the period rolls.

hours.title: Hours that respect the real calendar
hours.body: Weekly rules, split shifts, date overrides, buffers, min notice, daily caps. Conflict-checked against Google Calendar.

page.title: A hosted page. Your URL.
page.body: schedflow.com/{org}/{event} — timezone picker, month grid, questions, then confirm or pay. Pro can hide the badge.

embed.title: Or drop it on the site you already have
embed.body: Inline embed or a popup button. Same booking flow, no second design system to maintain.

1.title: Stand up an event type
1.body: Duration, location, buffers, custom questions. Leave it free, attach a price, or require an active membership.

2.title: Share the page — or embed it
2.body: Copy your hosted link, or drop the inline snippet on the site you already run. Invitees never create an account.

3.title: They pick a time in their zone
3.body: Slots are computed in UTC, shown in the invitee’s IANA timezone, DST-safe. Days without openings stay disabled.

4.title: Collect payment in the same motion
4.body: If the event is priced, we hold the slot and send them to Stripe Checkout on your Connect account. No PAN on our servers.

5.title: Calendar and email take it from there
5.body: Confirmation, .ics, Google write-back, 24h and 1h reminders. Reschedule and cancel from signed links in the email.

1.title: Hold the interval
1.body: A paid slot is reserved for 15 minutes so two people cannot checkout for the same hour.

2.title: Checkout on Stripe
2.body: Invitees pay through Stripe Checkout on your connected Express account. SchedFlow never sees the card number.

3.title: Confirm — or release
3.body: Payment success confirms the booking. If Checkout is abandoned, the hold expires and the time is bookable again.

4.title: Payouts on Connect
4.body: Express onboarding. Funds land on your connected account. SchedFlow takes a 2% application fee on those charges, not on your Pro subscription.

featuresPage.metaDescription: Event types, availability, hosted booking, Stripe payments, memberships, embeds, notifications, and a developer API.
featuresPage.title: Everything required to get booked and paid.
featuresPage.lead: Not a kitchen sink. The MVP is the loop independents actually run: publish hours, take the booking, collect the fee, send the invite, let people move it.

scheduling.title: Availability that behaves like a practice, not a spreadsheet
scheduling.body: Each host gets weekly rules, split shifts, and date overrides in an IANA timezone. Event types add buffers, minimum notice, max days ahead, and a daily cap. Slots are generated in UTC; the invitee picks in their own zone.
points: Google Calendar conflict check and write-back
Google Meet links when that’s the location
Double-booking blocked in the database, not just the UI

payments.title: The booking is not done until the money is
payments.body: Attach a catalog price to an event type and the public flow changes: hold, Checkout, confirm. Cards stay on Stripe so we remain PCI SAQ A. Refunds and receipts live next to the booking, not in a second tool.

memberships.title: Credits that refill when the period does
memberships.body: Tutors, trainers, and clinics sell a recurring plan. The customer gets N session credits per period, books credit-consuming event types without paying each time, and stops accruing when they cancel.
points: Period entitlement, not a punch card PDF
Dunning follows Stripe if a renewal fails
Dashboard balance next to booking history

presence.title: Hosted page, embed, same spine
presence.body: The public booking UI is server-rendered with the org’s brand color and logo. Embed mode strips the chrome so it sits inside an existing site. Pro can hide “Powered by SchedFlow”.
points: Guest checkout — no customer accounts in MVP
Signed links to manage, reschedule, cancel, pay

developers.title: API keys and signed webhooks, when you outgrow the dashboard
developers.body: Pro unlocks REST v1. Create bookings from a CRM, listen for booking.created, retry on HMAC-signed deliveries. The dashboard is enough until it isn’t.
points: API keys shown once at creation
Same tenancy rules as the UI

homeFaqs.q: Can I take paid bookings on the free plan?
homeFaqs.a: No. Free is for scheduling: three event types, one member, Google Calendar, and unpaid bookings. Pro unlocks Stripe Connect, pay-per-booking, memberships, branding, and the API.

homeFaqs.q: Do you ever store card numbers?
homeFaqs.a: Never. Invitees pay through Stripe Checkout on your connected account. SchedFlow stays in PCI SAQ A — no PAN on our servers.

homeFaqs.q: What if someone doesn’t finish paying?
homeFaqs.a: A paid slot is held for 15 minutes. If Checkout doesn’t complete, the hold expires and the time is bookable again.

homeFaqs.q: Do my clients need an account?
homeFaqs.a: Not in this release. Invitees book as guests, then manage, reschedule, or cancel from signed links in email.

homeFaqs.q: Can I embed booking on my own site?
homeFaqs.a: Yes. Inline embed or a popup button, same booking flow as the hosted page. Pro can hide the SchedFlow badge.
Not in the MVP. You can stay on Free indefinitely, upgrade self-serve when you need payments, and cancel in the Stripe customer portal. You remain Pro until the period ends.

pricingFaqs.a: The annual Stripe price is two months free versus paying monthly. Prices live in Stripe — we can change them without a code deploy.

On payments your clients make through Stripe Connect (one-off sessions and memberships), SchedFlow takes 200 basis points. Your Pro subscription is billed separately on our platform account and does not take that fee.

pricingFaqs.q: What happens if I cancel Pro?
pricingFaqs.a: You keep Pro until the period ends, then return to Free. Over-limit event types remain visible but you cannot create new ones. Paid event types stop accepting paid bookings.

pricingFaqs.q: Can I invoice enterprise or sign an annual contract?
pricingFaqs.a: Not yet. MVP is 100% self-serve: Free or Pro, monthly or yearly, via Stripe Checkout.
Connect onboarding starts with US, CA, GB, AU, IE, DE, FR, NL, ES, and IT. We expand from there.
